channel.title: The Quietus – Album of the Week
channel.description: Album of the Week reviews from The Quietus.

item.title: Put Your Hands In The Air: English Dancing Master by Leo Chadburn & Phaedra Ensemble
item.description: Leo Chadburn's latest work expands outwards from a seventeenth-century manual of folk dances to a kinetic exploration of human movement, from St Vitus' chorea to raving at Castlemorton Common

item.title: Tally Ho! Hark Away! Everything in Readiness by Shovel Dance Collective
item.description: The London experimental folk outliers’ triumphant third album is a demonstration of traditional music at its most progressive, outward-looking and migratory

item.title: Cities in Motion: Parallel Commutator by CZN
item.description: The third album to feature Valentina Magaletti in as many weeks finds the tireless rhythmic innovator teaming up with sculptor and gong-maker João Pais Filipe plus producer Leon Marks for an album of clattering polyrhythms and subtle synth washes

item.title: Move Any Mountain: Ako Akas by 10LEC6
item.description: Eight years after Bone Bame, the Paris collective return with a record named after a Cameroonian mountain that traps walkers in a dance they cannot quit. The reason they chose that story is more pointed than the sleeve lets on

item.title: Album of the Week: Vanishing Twin’s Archives
item.description: Absence makes the art grow bolder says Will Ainsley about Archives, which sounds like Chiastic Slide-era Autechre reimagining the Wicker Man soundtrack

item.title: Shared Frequency: Quiet Storm by Space Afrika
item.description: Manchester duo go big, vastly expanding their palette with strings, harps and a plethora of special guests

item.title: Not the How But the What: Lummernikt by Finn Loxbo
item.description: For all its stunning virtuosity, the tumbling fingerstyle guitar of Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo is always in service to a set of brilliant compositional ideas

item.title: The Beautiful World: Yours Sincerely by Haruomi Hosono
item.description: At 79 years old, the former Yellow Magic Orchestra and Happy End member has produced a true labour of love, offering a sometimes croonsome window on the sunlit uplands
